lines.text: This is why you can't drive from Alaska to Argentina.
cap: This is why you can't drive

lines.text: The Pan-American Highway runs from Prudhoe Bay in Alaska to Ushuaia in Argentina: about 30,000 kilometres, the longest road in the world.
lines.say: The Pan-American Highway runs from Prudhoe Bay in Alaska to Ushuaia in Argentina. About thirty thousand kilometres. The longest road in the world.
cap: runs from Prudhoe Bay in Alaska
the longest road in the world

lines.text: But between Panama and Colombia, it simply stops. For 106 kilometres, there is no road at all: the Darién Gap.
lines.say: But between Panama and Colombia, it simply stops. For one hundred and six kilometres, there is no road at all. The Darien Gap.
cap: there is no road at all

lines.text: In 1960, an expedition tried to drive across it anyway. It took them 136 days: about 200 metres an hour.
lines.say: In nineteen sixty, an expedition tried to drive across it anyway. It took them one hundred and thirty-six days. About two hundred metres an hour.
cap: tried to drive across it anyway

lines.text: So why is there no road? Can you guess?
cap: So why is there no road?

lines.text: Huge mountains, dense rainforest, and a swamp 80 kilometres wide.
lines.say: Huge mountains. Dense rainforest. And a swamp eighty kilometres wide.
